question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it be community/experimental support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: Current evidence shows an external FreeBSD port exists, but OpenClaw core still lacks the docs, installer, service, release-validation, and ownership contract needed for official Tier 1 support.

options.title: Define community FreeBSD scope
options.body: Keep the issue open and document FreeBSD as community/experimental only if maintainers want to acknowledge the existing port without owning Tier 1 support.

options.title: Promote toward Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD ownership and open tracked implementation work for installer/update behavior, rc.d/service management, docs, CI, and release validation.

options.title: Decline official support
options.body: Close if maintainers decide the existing FreeBSD ports/pkg path should remain external and unsupported by OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Define community FreeBSD scope
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and document FreeBSD as community/experimental only if maintainers want to acknowledge the existing port without owning Tier 1 support.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is the product support contract and long-term platform ownership, and CONTRIBUTING.md identifies steipete as the project lead.
